newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO head to meet Russia's Primakov.
newsitem.headline: NATO head to meet Russia's Primakov.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana will meet Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov in Vienna on September 20 as part of efforts to forge closer ties between the two Cold War foes, NATO diplomats said on Friday.
Solana last met Primakov in May in Berlin, but since then contacts were effectively frozen during the reelection campaign of President Boris Yeltsin.

Moscow has been vigorously opposed to NATO plans to expand its membership to take in new countries from eastern and central Europe, but has recently indicated it does not want the issue to stand in the way of a new NATO-Russia relationship.
On Thursday, NATO countries examined proposals for a special charter with Russia taking in all aspects of relations between the two former Cold War foes.
"The allies are all keen on trying to set up some form of mechanism that allows Moscow to have some form of hot-line in NATO headquarters," said one senior diplomat.
No decisions were taken at the informal meeting, but sources said the ambassadors would return to the subject in formal session over the next few weeks.
Senior alliance sources say a special heads of government summit is likely to be held in the spring or summer of 1997 to endorse both enlargement and a new deal with Moscow.
"The two things are separate but of course they are linked," said one official.
